newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso pares losses, but still weak on Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso pares losses, but still weak on Brazil.

text.p: The Mexican peso had trimmed some initial losses, but was still sharply weaker due to investors shedding peso instruments under impact from plunging Brazilian equities and weakness on the U.S. long bond, traders said.
"Dealers are keeping a close eye on Brazil," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart plummeted 4.5 and 5.1 centavos, respectively, to 7.9010/7.9030 and 7.8970/7.9000 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts had meanwhile closed trade for the day 3.9 centavos firmer at 7.8830/7.8880 per dollar.
"The peso has been very volatile, we saw massive speculation this morning, but the peso is getting back on its feet now," another trader said.
The Bovespa index of blue chips traded in Sao Paulo was meanwhile down 4.62 percent to 11,186 points. Earlier, however, the bolsa had been down over eight percent.
U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds were down 15/32 to yield 6.53 percent.
Dealers said the peso was also weakened by rising U.S. long bond yields.
The 30-year Treasury bond was down 13/32 to yield 6.52 percent.
Same-day peso contracts closed mid-morning 3.9 centavos weaker at 7.8830/7.8880 per dollar.
Dealers predicted further peso volatility next week.
"Some players who have lost money in recent days will try to recoup something before the month closes, and Brazil fallout looks as though it is not over yet," a trader said.
